source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed building accessibility checks

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
2. Identify the specific building location and areas inspected, noting the date and time of the inspection, and the name(s) of the inspector(s) involved.
3. Document the serial number and model of any equipment or tools used during the inspection process.
4. List the different accessibility standards and regulations that the building should comply with (e.g., ADA, local building codes).
5. Detail each failed accessibility check, describing the specific violation and area of the building:
   a. Use precise measurements (e.g., doors not being wide enough for wheelchair access, lack of ramps, including dimensions, slopes, and handrail heights).
   b. Note any visual or auditory accessibility issues (e.g., improper signage, absence of Braille, lack of visual or auditory emergency alarms).
   c. Include relevant photos or sketches to better illustrate the issue.
6. For each failed check, reference the specific section(s) of the applicable accessibility standards.
7.
